note: Jurisdiction as 'which legal system governs this finding and what defence exists here', not panorama trivia. The panorama and publicity columns are unchanged from the original six-country table so existing risk banding is untouched; the other dimensions are additive. Verify against primary sources before relying on any of it — sloppy law is worse than no law.

jurisdictions.name: United States
jurisdictions.authority: 17 U.S.C. §120(a) — pictorial representation exemption covers architectural works only
jurisdictions.parody_authority: Campbell v. Acuff-Rose Music, 510 U.S. 569 (1994) — parody may be fair use under §107
jurisdictions.exceptions_authority: 17 U.S.C. §107 — an open-ended four-factor standard, not a closed list
jurisdictions.incidental_authority: No statutory exception. De minimis is judge-made: Sandoval v. New Line (2d Cir. 1998) vs Ringgold v. BET (2d Cir. 1997)
jurisdictions.moral_authority: 17 U.S.C. §106A (VARA) — visual art only, attribution and integrity, waivable
jurisdictions.personal_data: State right of publicity (commercial appropriation); no general federal data-protection regime for video
jurisdictions.defamation_authority: New York Times v. Sullivan, 376 U.S. 254 (1964) — actual malice required for public figures

jurisdictions.name: United Kingdom
jurisdictions.authority: CDPA 1988 s.62 — buildings, sculptures and works of artistic craftsmanship on public display
jurisdictions.parody_authority: CDPA 1988 s.30A — caricature, parody or pastiche, added by SI 2014/2356
jurisdictions.exceptions_authority: CDPA 1988 ss.28-76 — fair dealing applies only to enumerated purposes
jurisdictions.incidental_authority: CDPA 1988 s.31 — incidental inclusion of a work in an artistic work, film or broadcast
jurisdictions.moral_authority: CDPA 1988 ss.77-85 — paternity must be asserted; rights are waivable
jurisdictions.personal_data: UK GDPR and Data Protection Act 2018 — an identifiable person in published footage is personal data
jurisdictions.defamation_authority: Defamation Act 2013 — serious-harm threshold, but historically claimant-friendly

jurisdictions.name: Germany
jurisdictions.authority: UrhG §59 (Panoramafreiheit) — works permanently in public ways or open places
jurisdictions.parody_authority: UrhG §51a — caricature, parody and pastiche, in force since 2021 (replacing free use under old §24)
jurisdictions.exceptions_authority: UrhG §§44a-63a — an enumerated catalogue of permitted uses; no general fair use
jurisdictions.incidental_authority: UrhG §57 — incidental works of minor significance alongside the actual subject
jurisdictions.moral_authority: UrhG §§12-14 — publication, attribution and integrity; inalienable, lasting as long as copyright
jurisdictions.personal_data: GDPR plus KunstUrhG §22 — publication of a person's image generally requires consent
jurisdictions.defamation_authority: StGB §§185-187 — insult and defamation are criminal offences

jurisdictions.name: France
jurisdictions.authority: CPI art. L.122-5 11° — panorama exception limited to non-commercial use by natural persons
jurisdictions.parody_authority: CPI art. L.122-5 4° — parodie, pastiche et caricature, subject to the rules of the genre
jurisdictions.exceptions_authority: CPI art. L.122-5 — an exhaustive list of exceptions; no general fair use
jurisdictions.incidental_authority: Théorie de l'accessoire — judge-made, narrow, and not a statutory exception
jurisdictions.moral_authority: CPI art. L.121-1 — droit moral is perpetual, inalienable and imprescriptible; it survives sale of the copyright
jurisdictions.personal_data: GDPR plus droit à l'image under Code civil art. 9 — consent is generally required
jurisdictions.defamation_authority: Loi du 29 juillet 1881 — diffamation is a criminal offence with short limitation periods

jurisdictions.name: Japan
jurisdictions.authority: Copyright Act art. 46 — artistic works permanently installed in open places
jurisdictions.parody_authority: No statutory parody exception. The Parody Montage case (Supreme Court, 1980) treated unauthorised parody as infringement of the integrity right
jurisdictions.exceptions_authority: Copyright Act arts. 30-50 — enumerated limitations only
jurisdictions.incidental_authority: Copyright Act art. 30-2 — incidental inclusion when creating a photographic or audiovisual work
jurisdictions.moral_authority: Copyright Act arts. 18-20 — publication, attribution and integrity; personal to the author
jurisdictions.personal_data: APPI (Act on the Protection of Personal Information), plus a judge-made right of likeness
jurisdictions.defamation_authority: Penal Code art. 230 — defamation is a criminal offence regardless of truth in principle

jurisdictions.name: India
jurisdictions.authority: Copyright Act s.52(1)(s)-(t) — sculpture/architecture permanently situated in a public place
jurisdictions.parody_authority: No parody exception. s.52(1)(a)(ii) covers criticism or review, which parody may or may not fall within — an argument, not a safe harbour
jurisdictions.exceptions_authority: Copyright Act s.52 — an exhaustive list of fair dealings; there is no general fair use
jurisdictions.incidental_authority: Copyright Act s.52(1)(u) — inclusion in a cinematograph film of an artistic work by way of background or incidentally. Notably generous, and it covers ARTISTIC works only, not music
jurisdictions.moral_authority: Copyright Act s.57 — author's special rights of attribution and integrity
jurisdictions.personal_data: DPDP Act 2023 (Digital Personal Data Protection) — consent-based regime; distinct from the US right of publicity
jurisdictions.defamation_authority: IPC §§499-500 (now BNS) — defamation is both a civil wrong and a criminal offence

jurisdictions.name: Canada
jurisdictions.authority: Copyright Act s.32.2(1)(b) — reproduction of architectural works and permanently-situated sculptures in public
jurisdictions.parody_authority: Copyright Act s.29 — parody and satire added as fair-dealing purposes by the Copyright Modernization Act, 2012
jurisdictions.exceptions_authority: Copyright Act ss.29-32.2 — fair dealing applies only to enumerated purposes, though read liberally since CCH (2004)
jurisdictions.incidental_authority: Copyright Act s.30.7 — incidental and not deliberate inclusion in another work
jurisdictions.moral_authority: Copyright Act ss.14.1-14.2 — integrity and attribution; may be waived but not assigned
jurisdictions.personal_data: PIPEDA, plus provincial privacy torts and Quebec Civil Code art. 36
jurisdictions.defamation_authority: Common-law defamation with a responsible-communication defence (Grant v. Torstar, 2009)

jurisdictions.name: Australia
jurisdictions.authority: Copyright Act 1968 ss.65-68 — buildings, sculptures and works of artistic craftsmanship in public places
jurisdictions.parody_authority: Copyright Act 1968 ss.41A and 103AA — fair dealing for parody or satire, added in 2006
jurisdictions.exceptions_authority: Copyright Act 1968 ss.40-43 — enumerated fair-dealing purposes only
jurisdictions.incidental_authority: Copyright Act 1968 s.67 — incidental filming of artistic works
jurisdictions.moral_authority: Copyright Act 1968 Part IX — attribution and integrity; consent may be given, rights may not be assigned
jurisdictions.personal_data: Privacy Act 1988 — Australia has no general tort of privacy and no right of publicity
jurisdictions.defamation_authority: Uniform Defamation Acts with a serious-harm element since 2021

jurisdictions.name: Brazil
jurisdictions.authority: Lei 9.610/98 art. 48 — works permanently situated in public places may be freely represented
jurisdictions.parody_authority: Lei 9.610/98 art. 47 — paraphrases and parodies that are not true reproductions and do not discredit the work. Narrower than it sounds
jurisdictions.exceptions_authority: Lei 9.610/98 art. 46 — an exhaustive and famously restrictive list
jurisdictions.incidental_authority: Lei 9.610/98 art. 46 VIII — incidental use of works in a larger work, provided it is not the main subject
jurisdictions.moral_authority: Lei 9.610/98 arts. 24-27 — moral rights are inalienable and unwaivable
jurisdictions.personal_data: LGPD (Lei 13.709/2018), plus image rights under Civil Code arts. 20-21
jurisdictions.defamation_authority: Código Penal arts. 138-140 — calúnia, difamação and injúria are criminal offences

jurisdictions.name: South Korea
jurisdictions.authority: Copyright Act art. 35(2) — works permanently exhibited in open places, subject to commercial-use limits
jurisdictions.parody_authority: No statutory parody exception. Art. 35-5 provides a fair-use-style general clause that may cover it — an argument, not a safe harbour
jurisdictions.exceptions_authority: Copyright Act arts. 23-35-5 — an enumerated list plus a general fair-use clause added in 2011
jurisdictions.incidental_authority: Copyright Act art. 35-3 — incidental inclusion when photographing or recording
jurisdictions.moral_authority: Copyright Act arts. 11-13 — disclosure, attribution and integrity; personal to the author
jurisdictions.personal_data: PIPA (Personal Information Protection Act) — among the strictest regimes globally, with a statutory right of publicity since 2022
jurisdictions.defamation_authority: Criminal Act arts. 307-309 — defamation is criminal even where the statement is true

jurisdictions.name: Spain
jurisdictions.authority: TRLPI art. 35.2 — works permanently situated in parks, streets, squares or other public thoroughfares
jurisdictions.parody_authority: TRLPI art. 39 — parody of a disclosed work, provided there is no risk of confusion and no damage to the work or author
jurisdictions.exceptions_authority: TRLPI arts. 31-40bis — an enumerated list; no general fair use
jurisdictions.incidental_authority: TRLPI art. 35.1 — works incidentally included in reporting on current events
jurisdictions.moral_authority: TRLPI art. 14 — moral rights are inalienable and unwaivable; integrity and attribution survive indefinitely
jurisdictions.personal_data: GDPR plus LOPDGDD, and the honour/image right under Ley Orgánica 1/1982
jurisdictions.defamation_authority: Código Penal arts. 205-216 — calumnia and injuria are criminal offences

jurisdictions.name: Italy
jurisdictions.authority: No freedom-of-panorama exception in the Legge sul diritto d'autore (L. 633/1941). Publication of images of cultural property for commercial purposes additionally requires authorisation from the Ministry of Culture under the Codice dei beni culturali (D.Lgs. 42/2004 arts. 107-108)
jurisdictions.parody_authority: No statutory parody exception. Courts have permitted parody via freedom of expression and the elaborazione creativa doctrine — an argument, not a safe harbour
jurisdictions.exceptions_authority: L. 633/1941 arts. 65-71decies — an enumerated list; no general fair use
jurisdictions.incidental_authority: No general incidental-inclusion exception; art. 70 permits limited quotation for criticism or discussion
jurisdictions.moral_authority: L. 633/1941 arts. 20-24 — moral rights are inalienable and may be asserted by heirs without time limit
jurisdictions.personal_data: GDPR plus Codice Privacy (D.Lgs. 196/2003), and image rights under Civil Code art. 10
jurisdictions.defamation_authority: Codice Penale art. 595 — diffamazione is a criminal offence, aggravated when committed through the press
